claims.text: CrFeCoNiAl, CrFeCoNiSi, and CrFeCoNiMn can each be prepared as single-phase solid solutions for the proposed comparison.
Oxidation above 900 °C promotes preferential surface segregation of Cr and Al in CrFeCoNiAl.
Cr and Al enrichment at the surface of CrFeCoNiAl drives formation of a continuous alumina-rich or spinel-type scale.
The oxide-metal interface produced on CrFeCoNiAl has low lattice mismatch.
Low oxide-metal lattice mismatch reduces internal stresses in the scale.
Reduced internal stress prevents cracking and spallation of the CrFeCoNiAl oxide scale.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn lack segregation comparable to the proposed beneficial Cr-Al segregation in CrFeCoNiAl.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn form less-adherent oxide scales that are prone to cracking and spallation.
High-temperature oxidation involves inward oxygen transport and outward Cr and Al transport.
Alumina has high thermodynamic stability relative to oxides of the other candidate alloying elements.
The low diffusivity and thermodynamic stability of alumina minimize stress accumulation.
A continuous alumina-rich scale grows slowly and remains protective.
Under identical 900–1100 °C oxidation conditions, CrFeCoNiAl will exhibit a more continuous scale and less cracking or spallation than CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn.
The proposed behavior is applicable to oxidizing or corrosive service between 900 and 1100 °C under laboratory-controlled conditions.
Real-time high-temperature measurement resolution limits determination of diffusion kinetics and interfacial stress relaxation.
Failure of CrFeCoNiAl to outperform the Si- and Mn-containing controls in scale coherence and cracking would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe preferential Cr and Al segregation leading to a stable alumina-rich oxide would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator permits either an alumina-rich or a spinel-type protective scale, but the falsification rule requires a stable alumina-rich oxide. A coherent protective spinel scale could therefore satisfy the stated mediator while triggering the stated falsification condition.
The hypothesis is stated for temperatures greater than 900 °C, while the experimental range includes 900 °C exactly.
